data.name: Vivaan
data.gender_notes: Vivaan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vivaan is a Sanskrit name meaning 'Bringer of life'. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'viv', which means 'to live'. This name is often given to a baby born after the loss of a previous child, as it is believed to bring new life and joy to the family. The name Vivaan carries the meaning “Bringer of life” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Vivaan usually hope their child will grow to embody bringer of life and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Vivaan is a powerful name that signifies the essence of life and the joy it brings. It is a name that is deeply rooted in Hindu spirituality and is often used to honor the cycle of life and the joy it brings. It is a name that inspires hope and new beginnings.
data.etymology: Vivaan belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Bringer of life.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vivaan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

vedic_reference.note: Derived from the Sanskrit root 'vi' (to go, to do) and 'van' (dwelling, abode). In Hindu mythology, Vivaan is the name of a divine messenger, a form of the god Vishnu.

historical_references.reference: Vivaan is mentioned as the name of a king in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, who ruled the kingdom of Haihayas. He is the eldest son of King Shatrasena and is also known as Vindhyaasura. Vivaan's most notable contribution is the construction of a bridge across the river Ganga to enable the army of the Pandava brothers to cross it and reach their kingdom.

Vivaan also appears in Jain literature as a legendary king who ruled over Magadha. He is considered an embodiment of the Jain Tirthankara, Bhagavan Mahavira, in his royal form. According to Jain texts, Vivaan ruled justly and was deeply devoted to knowledge and spiritual growth.
